articles.title: ‘Not really the thing to take a victory lap in’: the meaning of Jensen Huang’s new jacket
articles.summary: Nvidia’s boss has returned in a new uniform. But what does swapping leather for cotton say about power and leadership? • Don’t get Fashion Statement delivered to your inbox? Sign up here. It’s been a big week for the stock market and the leather jacket-wearing community.
body: Nvidia founder Jensen Huang, who had resigned as chief executive of the chipmaker after reports of multiple affairs, was reinstated as CEO. But as he returned to the company’s Silicon Valley headquarters surrounded by clapping employees chanting his name, one thing was amiss. Jensen was back, but the black leather jacket that had been his trademark piece for nearly two decades remained absent from its former power position. In its place? A navy cotton jacket.

articles.title: How Costume Designer Trish Summerville Reimagined ’70s Hollywood Style for ‘The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth’
articles.summary: From custom-printing vintage shirts for Brad Pitt to channeling Lauren Hutton for Elizabeth Debicki, the longtime David Fincher collaborator breaks down the film’s lived-in ’70s wardrobe.
body: Quentin Tarantino ’s Once Upon a Time in Hollywood is rich in striking, darkly memorable imagery: Margot Robbie shimmying in a sunshine-yellow two-piece at the Playboy Mansion; the sunbaked menace of Brad Pitt’s visit to the Manson ranch; the audaciously bloody denouement, all pit bulls and flamethrowers, playing out high in the Hollywood Hills, with the glittering carpet of nighttime Los Angeles extending endlessly beyond.

But for some—this writer included—the film’s most indelible legacy is its costumes. And, more specifically, those of Pitt’s laid-back (and possibly wife-murdering) stuntman Cliff Booth. Double-denim layers, gold-rimmed aviators, scuffed moccasins—and, of course, those Hawaiian shirts—the character’s late-’60s California cool burnt up the screen and almost certainly played a part in the Americana wave that plenty of menswear fanatics are still riding.

articles.title: The Body and The Teen Drama Fashion Machine
articles.summary: Coming-of-age series continue to flood streaming services. For fashion brands and resale platforms, they’re no longer a marketing pillar, but a fully fledged positioning strategy.
body: The Body, Overcompensating, Off Campus … Just when you thought pop culture had reached peak teen drama, the streaming giants release another slew of bingeable shows to capture the hearts of Gen Z and Gen Alpha viewers, and new audiences for their sponsors.

Taking the lion’s share of views at the moment is The Body, a coming-of-age psychodrama set in a Catholic school, which has quickly made its way into fashion fans’ For You pages. Just this week, the Netflix show has amassed 9.5 million views, marking its second week in the platform’s global top 10. It’s also currently the number one show in 39 countries.

Costumed by Mirren Gordon-Crozier, the series features iconic ‘00s designs, including the Dior Saddle bag, a Louis Vuitton x Takashi Murakami Pochette, a John Galliano-era “J’adore Dior” T-shirt, and various Juicy Couture accessories.
points: For fashion brands and resale platforms, they’re no longer a marketing pillar, but a fully fledged positioning strategy.

articles.title: The Art of Being Veruschka: Fashion Pays Tribute to a Legend
articles.summary: Generations of fashion’s image-makers, designers, and models reflect on the late Veruschka: the woman who made modeling an art form of its own.
body: “There is and will always be only one Veruschka,” Richard Avedon wrote in the May 1972 issue of Vogue in an impassioned tribute to his muse. More than half a century later, his words still ring true. Since news broke of the German supermodel’s death at the age of 87, generations of fashion’s image-makers, designers, and models have been reflecting on her immeasurable influence.

A protagonist of some of the most fantastical fashion editorials ever committed to the pages of Vogue and a prolific cover star, Veruschka helped expand the possibilities of what a model could be. Her body was her artistic medium, her imagination as instrumental to the making of a photograph as that of the person behind the lens. Her creative curiosity would endure long after her heyday in the 1960s and ’70s, finding expression in her experiments with body painting and camouflage, her performance art, and her occasional, much-feted returns to the runway.
points: Generations of fashion’s image-makers, designers, and models reflect on the late Veruschka: the woman who made modeling an art form of its own.

articles.title: Kim and Khloé Kardashian’s Beauty Trip Didn’t Quite Go to Plan—Here’s What to Know Before Booking Yours
articles.summary: From vetting practitioners abroad to treatment stacking, experts weigh in on what to know before you go all-in on beauty tourism like the Kardashians.
body: Between the salmon sperm facials, the skin boosters, and the next generation of lasers, there’s plenty to pique the interest of the beauty obsessive in South Korea. So much so that vacations are increasingly being organized around visits to the dermatologist’s office. But how much is too much when it comes to our beauty itineraries? Just ask Khloé and Kim Kardashian.

On Wednesday’s episode of her podcast, Khloé in Wonder Land, Koko and her close friend La La Anthony reminisced about their August 2025 trip to South Korea, where they enthusiastically availed themselves of the country’s advanced cosmetic treatments—with some less-than-desirable results.

“Kim and I came back deformed, you came back beautiful and the plane ride just made it so much worse,” Kardashian told Anthony, recalling how their post-treatment appearances had kept them holed up in their hotel room.

articles.title: Striped Malted Pound Cake
articles.summary: Layering the malted vanilla and chocolate batters so they create a striped pattern isn’t just an aesthetic choice. Doing so really does keep the flavors distinct.
body: My earliest dessert obsession was the malted milkshake, which I indulged in every time I had enough babysitting money. My oldest, best friend, Toi, was equally obsessed with Whoppers, and we both wondered why malted sweets were so good. Turns out, the secret is in the combination of malted barley, wheat flour, and evaporated whole milk that gets toasted to caramelize the sugars contained in it.

I originally made this syrup to give my milkshakes that nostalgic, malt-shop flavor. But honey, it’s no one-hit wonder. It is a beautiful sweetener and is terrific when brushed on top of still-warm Striped Malted Pound Cake.

I also drizzle it over roasted fruit and mix it into buttercreams, glazes, and frostings. For breakfast, I stir it into coffee or lattes, smoothies, yogurt, and oatmeal. And it’s got savoy game, too. Try it on a dinner plate, spooned over roasted sweet potatoes or carrots alongside roasted chops or chicken.
Grease a 9x5" loaf pan with softened butter or cooking spray. Dust the pan with all-purpose flour, shaking out any excess.

articles.title: 11 Restaurants in NYC That Are Open on Christmas Day
articles.summary: Whether you’re looking for a prix fixe meal with reserve wine, or you want to find a spot that’ll fill the younger members of your party with a little holiday cheer.
body: Maybe you’re traveling to enjoy the singular experience of Rockefeller Center and the Rockettes at Christmas time, or you’re a local who’s spending the holidays at home. Regardless, this season is one of the most special times to spend in New York City, which makes it an exceptionally busy time of year for restaurants and bars alike.

Even with the foresight to make a reservation or two, it can be a challenge to find a place to enjoy lunch or dinner with a group on Christmas Day; many spots close for the day, while others simply don’t feel quite special enough for a true, New York City holiday. To help you avoid a last-minute scramble for a table or a less-than-festive dinner date, we’ve curated a guide of some of the very best restaurants open in NYC on Christmas day. Many of these spots will be serving their usual, outstanding menus, while some are offering holiday special cocktails, desserts, and entrées.
